1	# SignalScout AI
2	
3	**A B2B prospecting agent that checks its data, and its own claims, before it spends money or writes outreach.**
4	
5	Built for neatHack 2026 by Abhijit Manna and Garvit Mathur.
6	
7	| | |
8	|---|---|
9	| **Try it** | https://mindstack-neathack.vercel.app/live |
10	| **Demo video (3 min)** | <<VIDEO_URL>> |
11	| **Evidence page** | https://mindstack-neathack.vercel.app/results |
12	| **Business plan (cfo.ai)** | https://cfo.ai/s/FD45bXSO15ZacVmj |
13	| **Hackathon tools and proof** | [hackathon.md](hackathon.md) |
14	
15	## Try it in 30 seconds
16	
17	Open **/live**, paste a code, press **Run search**.
18	
19	| Code | What it runs | Limit |
20	|---|---|---|
21	| `D0GS-0TN7-T87V-72SE-02HN-N68S-FM28-GY60` | The full pipeline on synthetic fixture companies with a fake model. Nothing is spent. Your search criteria are ignored (the page says so). One draft deliberately contains an invented number, so you can watch the claim check suppress it. | 100 runs |
22	| `TGKK-AZBH-5N5D-EJDG-Z8BZ-C5FG-GTDH-NFYB` | A real run: Crustdata search and enrichment, then a real model. 10 companies, about 30 to 60 seconds. Company data in live runs is provided by Crustdata. | 1 run, first come first served. If it says no runs left, contact us: abhijitmanna912001@gmail.com |
23	
24	Live runs are invite only and sit behind a kill switch. Company data is shown in your browser only; our database stores counts and costs, never company records.
25	
26	## The idea
27	
28	Most prospecting tools spend first and check later: they pay to enrich junk records and write outreach that states things nobody verified. SignalScout does the checks first.
29	
30	1. **Validate and deduplicate before paying.** Rejected records and duplicates never reach paid enrichment.
31	2. **Assess from facts only.** Every field becomes a fact with a status and a source. Only `given` or `cross_checked` facts can be cited.
32	3. **Check the claims.** Every number in an outreach draft must appear in a cited fact. If it does not, the draft is suppressed.
33	
34	Pipeline: ICP, search, validate and deduplicate, enrich the best candidates within caps, build facts, assess, check claims.
35	
36	## Does it work? Baseline vs improved
37	
38	Same 10 records, same model (claude-haiku, temperature 0), one run per pipeline.
39	
40	| Synthetic fixtures with known defects | Baseline | Improved |
41	|---|---|---|
42	| Wasted enrichments | 1 | 0 |
43	| Valid companies enriched | 2 | 3 |
44	| Companies assessed | 10 | 5 |
45	| Model calls | 10 | 5 |
46	| Model cost | $0.0183 | $0.0120 |
47	| Outreach drafts with citation violations | 3 | 0 |
48	| Cited facts that cannot be cited | 4 | 0 |
49	
50	The same comparison on **10 real Crustdata records with the real model**: drafts with violations 4 vs 0, model cost $0.0272 vs $0.0194. On the real data, enrichment changed 3 of 5 companies from valid to flagged by a size rule, and only the improved pipeline re-validates after enrichment.
51	
52	These are small samples, one scenario and one run each. They show the mechanism, not a benchmark. Full tables: [docs/DETAILS.md](docs/DETAILS.md).
53	
54	**Verified live run on the deployed site (12 Oct 2026):** 10 searched, 5 enriched, 5 assessed, 0 failed. Provider cost estimate $3.69, which matches the 12.3 credits on Crustdata's usage page. Model cost estimate about $0.02 (our estimate; the model provider's usage page was not checked).
55	
56	## Hackathon tools
57	
58	| Tool | How we used it |
59	|---|---|
60	| **neatlogs** | Traces of the two official runs (`baseline-final`, `improved-final`). Markdown exports in [evidence/traces/](evidence/traces/). The improved trace shows the validation and guardrail spans. |
61	| **Entire** | Checkpoints on our Claude Code work. 34 `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers in the history. List and caveats in [hackathon.md](hackathon.md). |
62	| **cfo.ai** | [Business plan](https://cfo.ai/s/FD45bXSO15ZacVmj) built from measured unit costs: search $0.069 per record, enrichment $0.60 per company. Estimated contribution margin 60.10% at an assumed, unvalidated $40 per run. Excludes failed-job spend, tools and hosting, and salaries. |
63	| **Crustdata** | Company data for search and enrichment. Their team replied (informally, 12 Oct) that this invite-only use is fine and asked for an attribution line, which the live page shows. |
64	
65	## What protects the spend (and what does not)
66	
67	- Caps on records searched, enrichments and model calls; a budget guard before every paid call.
68	- Invite codes are stored as hashes; one run at a time per code; per-IP rate limits; a database kill switch that is off by default.
69	- No export or download feature, and at most 10 companies per run.
70	- Our database stores no company records. During a live run, search filters and LinkedIn URLs go to Crustdata, and facts from the results go to the model provider for scoring. We make no claim about what they retain.
71	
72	## Honest limits
73	
74	- Fixtures are synthetic, there is one scenario, and each result is a single run.
75	- Flagged companies come from a zero-tolerance size rule whose magnitude we did not analyse: a rule outcome, not proof that the data is wrong.
76	- Live costs are estimates. There is no dollar cap per run: the protection is the record and call caps, the per-code run limit and the Crustdata key's own budget.
77	- The model endpoint for live runs is Anthropic's OpenAI-compatible layer, which Anthropic documents as a testing layer. `claude-haiku-4-5` has a tentative retirement date not sooner than 15 October 2026.
78	- The home page form only records a profile. The pipeline runs on `/live` and `/results`.
79	
80	Everything else, including the full limitations list, is in [docs/DETAILS.md](docs/DETAILS.md).
81	
82	## Run it
83	
84	```bash
85	npm install
86	npm run dev                       # http://localhost:3000, results at /results
87	npm test                          # 829 tests pass; 6 skip without a database
88	npx tsx scripts/run-pipeline.ts --pipeline improved --trace off   # free: fixtures, fake model
89	```
90	
91	Runs that spend money need `--confirm-spend`; see [docs/DETAILS.md](docs/DETAILS.md#run-it).
92	
93	## More
94	
95	- [docs/DETAILS.md](docs/DETAILS.md): how the guards work, all tables, safety controls, live beta setup, tests, layout, full limitations
96	- [docs/BUILD_LOG.md](docs/BUILD_LOG.md): build log and the full Entire checkpoint table
97	- `evidence/`: `summary.json` and the neatlogs trace exports
